name: Axion-to-Photon Conversion in a Dielectric (Problem 8a — gemini)

problem.fidelity: problem-definition only; solutions appendix not consulted

regime: zero-temperature non-magnetic solid dielectric, no external electric field, natural units hbar=c=1

conventions.interaction: L=-(g/4) a F Fdual, vertex validated against vacuum a->gg width g^2 m^3/64pi
conventions.rate: single-axion disappearance rate Gamma=-ImPi/omega on shell (Caputo et al. convention)
conventions.response: dressed longitudinal propagator D00=1/(q^2 eps_L); absorptive weight (2/q^2) Im[-1/eps_L]
conventions.photon: outgoing transverse photon with |q|=n w in the given-n approximation; recoil neglected
conventions.photon_measure: free-photon cut normalized as 2pi delta(q^2) with the 1/(2|q|) Jacobian; the given-n dispersion enters only in the on-shell relation; the stated model does not fix the in-medium spectral-density normalization (see limitation prefactor_normalization)

requested_outputs.description: Gamma_NR for m_a = 25 eV in eV
Gamma_NR for m_a = 15 eV in eV

claims.title: general closed-form rate Gamma(Ea,ka) with angular factor J(k)
NR specialization with exact-rational skeleton and bounded finite-kappa correction

obligations.statement: tensor contraction giving |q x p|^2 vertex structure

obligations.evidence_required: KKL response identity + D00 relation + sum-rule check

obligations.statement: threshold gate Ea > wp at T=0

derivations.description: Derivation of Gamma = g^2 wp qg^2 ka^2 J(kappa) / (16 pi Ea wg)
derivations.support: UNSUPPORTED — delta-distribution calculus, tensor contraction, phase-space integration have no PhysMath rules; derivation is pen-and-paper recorded in README.md

steps.description: aFF_dual coupling gives amplitude proportional to g epsilon^{mu nu rho sigma} k1_rho k2_sigma
|M|^2 proportional to g^2 |q x p|^2 via Levi-Civita contraction
Rate from optical theorem: Gamma = -Im Pi(omega)/omega
Insert Im[-1/eps_L] = (pi/2) wp delta(w-wp) for Im D00
p0 integral sets p0 = wp via medium delta
q integral fixes |q| = n(Ea-wp) = qg via on-shell delta
dOmega integral gives ka^2 J(kappa) closed form
combine all factors to Gamma = g^2 wp qg^2 ka^2 J(kappa) / (16 pi Ea wg)

solver_local_computations.conventions: NR kinematics: Ea = m(1+v^2/2), ka = mv; skeleton = g^2 wp qg^2 ka^2 / (6 Ea wg)
solver_local_computations.inputs: g, wp, n, va, m_a (all exact rationals)
solver_local_computations.independent_checks: float64 cross-check via GammaGeneral at same kinematics

solver_local_computations.outputs: correction factor C (float64, documented |C-1| < 1e-5 at benchmark)

solver_local_computations.independent_checks: GammaGeneral cross-check; dimensional scaling test; unit-slip sensitivity test

deviations.capability_sought: exact rational arithmetic for parameter substitution
deviations.api_examined: physmath.NewRational — constructs exact rational expressions in the PhysMath expression IR
deviations.reason: The PhysMath NewRational API produces expression-IR nodes, not Go big.Rat values suitable for direct arithmetic. The problem requires numerical evaluation (division, multiplication of many rationals into a scalar result), which PhysMath expression IR does not execute — evaluation is architecturally deferred (Arch §25, Spec §23.2). stdlib big.Rat provides the identical exact-rational capability for direct arithmetic without requiring the expression IR.
deviations.local_alternative: stdlib math/big.Rat with exact-decimal string constructors (ratFromString), performing the same exact arithmetic without the expression-IR layer

deviations.api_examined: PhysMath rule registry (9 rules: EXPR-CANON-001 through EXPR-APPLY-001); integral/1 family
deviations.reason: No PhysMath rule handles delta-distribution calculus or integration. The integral/1 family is REPRESENTATIONAL ONLY — no consuming rule exists. Delta-function collapse is a pen-and-paper operation with no PhysMath equivalent.
deviations.local_alternative: hand derivation recorded in README.md step 5; result hardcoded into the closed-form rate formula

deviations.capability_sought: tensor contraction with medium projector (Levi-Civita epsilon tensor)
deviations.api_examined: PhysMath tensor/1 family; no contraction rule in the 9-rule registry
deviations.reason: PhysMath represents tensors (tensor/1) but has no contraction rule. The Levi-Civita evaluation requires index contraction that is not executable.
deviations.local_alternative: hand derivation recorded in README.md step 2; independently checked by numeric evaluation

deviations.capability_sought: phase-space integration (angular integral over solid angle)
deviations.reason: integral/1 is REPRESENTATIONAL ONLY — no rule evaluates integrals. The angular integral yielding J(kappa) must be computed outside PhysMath.
deviations.local_alternative: closed-form J(kappa) function in axion.JClosed; independently verified by Simpson quadrature in TestPrefactorAssembly

deviations.api_examined: phys-lib gr.NewFramework — hardcodes phys-gr namespace; no axion-electrodynamics domain package exists
deviations.reason: gr.NewFramework rejects non-GR assumption IDs (§14.3 anti-example). No phys-lib axion or dielectric package exists. Creating one would require human governance (Arch §27.5).
deviations.local_alternative: demo-local Assumption/Source records in axion package; growth-gate note in README.md

verification.executed: exact-rational parameter substitution and skeleton arithmetic; float64 closed-form evaluation; end-to-end phase-space assembly quadrature against the closed form under the documented convention; kappa=1 removable-singularity limit and domain-guard behavior; replayed nothing (no PhysMath derivations: delta-collapse, tensor contraction, and phase-space integration are unsupported by the rule registry)
verification.represented_only: analytical derivation steps, source mapping, assumption records, response model, normalization-convention statement, threshold reasoning

limitations.statement: No PhysMath rule executes any derivation step; the rule registry has no delta-distribution, tensor-contraction-with-projector, or phase-space-integration operation. Arithmetic is exact-rational Go, documented as numerical evaluation, not engine proof.
The q-independent plasmon-pole response is given by the problem; real materials have continua, gaps, dispersion, and local-field effects.

The rate prefactor 1/(16pi) is audited and reproduced by a cut/spectral-density assembly calibrated on the vacuum width (see README 'Assembly audit'), but the stated model fixes neither the in-medium photon spectral-density normalization nor, equivalently, one power of n. The quoted 1.31e-41 eV is conditional on the adopted convention (free massless cut 2pi delta(q^2) with the given-n dispersion in the on-shell relation); standard alternatives give 1/n ~ 0.67x or n = 1.5x the quoted value (8.7e-42 or 2.0e-41 eV), and the model as stated does not select among them.
The 15 eV result is exactly 0 by T=0 kinematics within the model, not by a computed cancellation.
No observational or experimental consequences are represented or claimed.
